vulnerability_title: [M-01] Vault owner is incetivized to not switch invalid collateral token, during liquidation

recommendation.recommendation_text:
In case the collateral token becomes invalid, liquidation should still require payments from the vault based on the same `vaultFactor` logic, rather than shifting the entire burden to the pool. This ensures agents remain properly incentivized to update their collateral token when governance decisions invalidate one.

**[Flare mitigated](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-10-flare-mitigation?tab=readme-ov-file#mitigation-of-high--medium-severity-issues):**

> Token deprecation and agent vault token switching have been removed.

**Status:** Mitigation confirmed. Full details in reports from [givn](https://code4rena.com/audits/2025-10-flare-fasset-mitigation-review/submissions/S-3), [rvierdiiev](https://code4rena.com/audits/2025-10-flare-fasset-mitigation-review/submissions/S-1), and [farman1094](https://code4rena.com/audits/2025-10-flare-fasset-mitigation-review/submissions/S-7).

content_code_consistency.content_reasoning: currentLiquidationFactorBIPS sets the vault share to zero when the vault collateral is invalid and the pool collateral is valid, so the pool pays the whole liquidation (lines 37-39). This is the rule the finding links to and builds its argument on. The cap that limits the agent's share of the pool payment is in LiquidationFacet.sol, so the second half of the argument cannot be checked here.
patterns_found: vault share set to zero when the vault collateral is invalid, so the pool pays everything
issues: The cap that makes the vault cover only half of the pool's payment is in LiquidationFacet.sol line 217, not in this file.
`vaultFactor` and `poolFactor` are the finding's names for `_c1FactorBIPS` and `_poolFactorBIPS`; the literal names do not occur in the file.

scsvs_classification.vulnerability_type: liquidation payment rule removes the incentive to replace invalid collateral
